title: Low Water Cutoff Tripped
shortDescription: The low water cutoff (LWCO) has detected insufficient water in the boiler and shut down the burner.
fullDescription:
Weil-McLain boilers use a low water cutoff safety device that stops the burner from firing if the water level in the boiler drops below a safe threshold. Firing a dry boiler can crack the heat exchanger and create a serious safety hazard.

Causes include a system leak, waterlogged expansion tank that caused water loss through the relief valve, a malfunctioning automatic feed valve, or a failed probe/float-type LWCO. On steam boilers, low water is often due to scaled probes or sediment in the float chamber.

On hydronic systems, pressure should read 12-15 psi when cold. If pressure is low, check for leaks before adding water.
safetyWarning: Do NOT bypass the low water cutoff. A dry-fired boiler can rupture and cause severe burns, property damage, or fire.

fixSteps.title: Check system pressure
fixSteps.instruction: On hydronic systems, verify cold pressure is 12-15 psi. If low, inspect for leaks at pumps, valves and relief valve discharge.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for visible leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Check around boiler, pumps, zone valves, and baseboards for water staining or active drips.

fixSteps.title: Add water carefully
fixSteps.instruction: If pressure is low and no leak is evident, slowly open the feed valve to bring pressure to 12 psi cold. Do not overfill.

fixSteps.title: Call a technician for repeat faults
fixSteps.instruction: If the LWCO trips again, a licensed tech should test/flush the probe or float chamber and diagnose hidden leaks.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

faq.q: Can I keep adding water if it loses pressure?
faq.a: No. Repeated make-up water introduces oxygen and minerals that destroy the boiler. Find the leak.

title: Ignition Failure - Burner Lockout
shortDescription: The boiler attempted ignition but failed to prove flame within the trial-for-ignition period.
fullDescription:
The ignition control attempts three trials for ignition. If flame is not sensed on the last attempt, the control locks out and cuts gas to the burner for safety. Common on Weil-McLain Ultra, WM97+, Evergreen and CGa/CGi series.

Likely causes: no gas (closed shutoff, empty LP tank, tripped gas meter), dirty flame rod, weak spark igniter, blocked venting (condensate or ice), or a failed gas valve. On condensing models, a plugged condensate trap can also cause ignition lockout due to blocked flue gas path.

Most ignition faults require resetting the boiler and diagnosing root cause before refiring.
safetyWarning: Gas present. Do not repeatedly reset a boiler that fails ignition - unburned gas can accumulate in the combustion chamber and vent system.

causes.cause: Dirty or oxidized flame sensor rod
Weak spark igniter or cracked electrode

fixSteps.title: Verify gas supply
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm gas shutoff valve is open and other gas appliances work. For LP, check tank level.

fixSteps.title: Reset once
fixSteps.instruction: Press reset on the control. If it locks out again, stop and call a technician - do not keep resetting.

fixSteps.title: Professional diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: Tech will clean flame rod, check igniter spark, measure microamps, check gas pressure, and inspect venting/condensate path.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

faq.q: How many times can I reset?
faq.a: Once. Repeated resets risk gas accumulation in the combustion chamber.

title: Blocked Vent or Air Intake
shortDescription: The pressure switch sensed inadequate flue draft, indicating a blocked vent, intake, or failed inducer.
fullDescription:
Weil-McLain condensing and induced-draft boilers use a differential pressure switch to confirm the combustion blower is pulling proper airflow through the heat exchanger. If the switch does not close (or opens during the call), the control prevents ignition.

Common causes are ice or snow blocking sidewall PVC vent terminals, debris or bird nests in the intake, disconnected pressure switch hose, water in the pressure switch hose or condensate trap, or a failing inducer motor.

Inspect both intake and exhaust terminations outside the building before assuming internal failure.
safetyWarning: Blocked vents can cause CO to spill into the home. Ensure CO detectors are operational and never operate a boiler with a compromised vent.
symptoms: Boiler tries to start, shuts off quickly

fixSteps.title: Clear vent terminations outside
fixSteps.instruction: Remove snow, ice, leaves, or nests from both intake and exhaust PVC terminations. Maintain 12+ inches clearance from snow line.

fixSteps.title: Check condensate trap
fixSteps.instruction: Clean the condensate trap per manufacturer instructions - blockage here can also trigger vent faults.

fixSteps.title: Professional service
fixSteps.instruction: If the fault persists, technician should check inducer amp draw, pressure switch operation, and hose integrity.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

faq.q: Why does this happen after every snowstorm?
faq.a: Sidewall vents need clear exterior space. Consider relocating or adding a vent guard.

title: High Limit / Overheat Lockout
shortDescription: Boiler water temperature exceeded the high limit, shutting down the burner for safety.
fullDescription:
When boiler supply temperature exceeds roughly 200-220F (depending on model/setpoint), the high limit aquastat or control cuts the burner to prevent steam flashing in a hot-water system.

Root causes typically involve poor heat transfer out of the boiler: stuck circulator, closed zone valves, air-bound system, undersized expansion tank causing pressure lockup, or a scaled heat exchanger. Low flow through the boiler during a firing cycle is the most common cause.

Reset is usually manual. Do not simply reset repeatedly - find the flow problem first.
safetyWarning: High-temperature water can flash to steam and cause severe burns. Do not loosen fittings on a hot system.

causes.cause: Closed zone valve or air-bound zone

symptoms: Boiler kicks off at high temperature

fixSteps.title: Let boiler cool
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off power and wait 30+ minutes for temperatures to drop before inspecting.

fixSteps.title: Check circulator operation
fixSteps.instruction: On a heat call, confirm the circulator is spinning and warm. A cold circulator during a call means stuck or failed.

fixSteps.title: Purge air from zones
fixSteps.instruction: Use purge valves or bleed screws to remove trapped air which blocks circulation.

fixSteps.title: Call a pro if unresolved
fixSteps.instruction: Technician should inspect expansion tank charge, heat exchanger, and limit control.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

faq.q: Why does the relief valve drip?
faq.a: High limit trip plus failing expansion tank causes pressure spikes that open the relief valve.

title: Gas Valve Electrical Fault
shortDescription: The ignition control does not sense proper coil resistance or feedback from the gas valve.
fullDescription:
The control monitors the gas valve coils and, on modulating boilers, the valve's position feedback signal. A bad coil, broken wire, or faulty valve triggers this code and locks out the burner.

On Weil-McLain Ultra / WM97+ / Evergreen modulating boilers, intermittent valve faults can also stem from loose harness pins or water intrusion into the valve assembly.
safetyWarning: Gas valve is a safety-critical component. Only a licensed gas technician should replace it.
symptoms: No gas flow even with call for heat

fixSteps.title: Call a licensed HVAC technician
fixSteps.instruction: Gas valve diagnosis requires combustion analyzer, manometer, and code-compliant replacement procedures.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

faq.q: Can I replace the gas valve myself?
faq.a: No - gas valve work requires a licensed professional and post-replacement combustion testing.

title: Water Pressure Sensor Out of Range
shortDescription: The water pressure transducer is reporting a value outside the valid range, or has failed.
fullDescription:
Modulating-condensing Weil-McLain boilers use a pressure transducer instead of a simple pressure switch. The control requires a valid pressure reading (typically 12-30 psi) to allow firing.

Causes: genuinely low system pressure (leak), clogged port at the sensor, disconnected connector, or a failed transducer. Pressure transducers can drift or short after several years of service.
safetyWarning: Low system pressure can lead to dry firing. Do not bypass the sensor.

fixSteps.title: Read pressure gauge
fixSteps.instruction: Compare the analog gauge to what the control displays. Major mismatch indicates sensor issue.

fixSteps.title: Check connector
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, reseat pressure sensor harness. Look for corrosion or water damage.

fixSteps.title: Replace transducer
fixSteps.instruction: A licensed tech should drain, replace, refill and re-pressurize the boiler.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

faq.q: Is this the same as LWCO?
faq.a: No - this is a pressure reading fault, LWCO is a water-level device.

title: Air Trapped in Hydronic System
shortDescription: Boiler detects abnormal temperature swings or flow issues consistent with air in the system.
fullDescription:
Air pockets cause cavitation at the circulator and dead zones at baseboards. The boiler can trigger delta-T faults or high limit cycling when a zone is air-bound.

Weil-McLain cast iron and condensing boilers should be purged at startup, after any service, and when fresh water is added. Automatic air vents on the boiler top should be operational.
safetyWarning: Use caution around hot water when purging - water can be scalding.

causes.cause: Air trapped after fill or repair

fixSteps.title: Bleed radiators/baseboards
fixSteps.instruction: Use bleed key on each radiator until water flows without sputtering.

fixSteps.title: Use purge valves
fixSteps.instruction: Isolate each zone and purge fresh water through the drain to push air out.

fixSteps.title: Replace air vent if leaking
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the automatic air vent on top of the boiler if it drips or fails to release air.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

faq.q: How often should I bleed radiators?
faq.a: Once a year at start of heating season, or whenever uneven heat appears.

title: Circulator Pump Not Running
shortDescription: Control energized the circulator but did not detect proper flow, or the pump is seized.
fullDescription:
The boiler relies on a circulator pump (internal on modulating units, external on cast iron) to move water through the heat exchanger. Without flow, the boiler overheats rapidly.

Causes: seized cartridge from years of scale, burned motor winding, bad relay on the control board, tripped breaker, or air bound pump. Replacing a sticky cartridge or switching to an ECM pump is a common repair.
safetyWarning: Boiler water is hot and under pressure. Shut off and cool before opening any service port.

fixSteps.title: Check breaker/power
fixSteps.instruction: Verify boiler breaker has not tripped and service switch is on.

fixSteps.title: Bleed the pump
fixSteps.instruction: On pumps with a bleed screw, crack open briefly to release air.

fixSteps.title: Tech replaces cartridge/pump
fixSteps.instruction: Professional will isolate, drain, and replace the pump or cartridge as needed.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

faq.a: 8-15 years depending on water quality and duty cycle.

title: Supply or Return Thermistor Open/Short
shortDescription: A water temperature thermistor (supply, return or flue) is reporting an invalid reading.
fullDescription:
Modulating boilers use 10K NTC thermistors at the supply, return, flue, DHW, and outdoor locations. An open or shorted sensor will lock the boiler out until replaced.

Check the specific fault on the display to identify which sensor. Values should read approximately 10K ohms at 77F. Out-of-range readings indicate a bad sensor or damaged wire.
safetyWarning: Power off the boiler before disconnecting sensors - line voltage may be nearby.

fixSteps.title: Identify faulted sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Read the display to confirm which thermistor is failing.

fixSteps.title: Tech measures and replaces
fixSteps.instruction: Technician ohms out the sensor per Weil-McLain resistance chart and replaces if out of spec.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

faq.a: Use Weil-McLain OEM sensors for proper fit and calibration.

title: Internal Control Module Fault
shortDescription: The boiler control has a self-diagnostic error - internal memory, relay, or communication fault.
fullDescription:
Weil-McLain boilers run continuous self-checks on the ignition control. This fault indicates a hardware-level failure: relay weld, EEPROM corruption, or loss of communication with the display module.

Power cycle can clear a transient error. Repeated control faults require replacement of the ignition module or display by a technician.
safetyWarning: Do not open the control enclosure while powered. Line voltage and gas valve control are inside.

causes.cause: Failed relay or IC on board

fixSteps.title: Power cycle boiler
fixSteps.instruction: Turn the boiler breaker off for 60 seconds, then on.

fixSteps.title: Technician replaces module
fixSteps.instruction: If fault returns, a licensed tech will replace the ignition control/display module.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

faq.q: Is a surge protector worth it?
faq.a: Yes - a whole-house or boiler-specific surge protector extends control board life.

title: Flame Lost During Run
shortDescription: Boiler ignited but flame was lost mid-cycle, causing safety shutdown.
fullDescription:
The flame rod should detect a microamp signal from rectification of flame conductivity. Loss of signal mid-run shuts the gas valve immediately.

Causes: oxidized flame rod, cracked porcelain, low gas pressure sag under demand, insufficient combustion air, or a partially blocked vent causing flame roll-out. On condensing boilers, flooded combustion chamber from a plugged drain can also extinguish the flame.
safetyWarning: Repeated flame loss may indicate unsafe combustion. Do not bypass the flame sensor.

fixSteps.title: Clean flame rod
fixSteps.instruction: Technician removes and gently cleans the rod with fine abrasive pad - no sandpaper.

fixSteps.title: Measure microamps
fixSteps.instruction: Micro-amps should be above 1.5uA typically. Low reading = replace rod.

fixSteps.title: Check gas pressure under load
fixSteps.instruction: Inlet gas pressure must hold within spec during firing.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

title: Return Water Temperature Fault
shortDescription: Return temp is outside allowed range (too low for non-condensing, or delta-T too high).
fullDescription:
On a cast iron Weil-McLain boiler, return water below ~130F causes flue gas condensation that destroys the heat exchanger. Some controls log this condition.

On modulating-condensing models, an excessive delta-T between supply and return (low flow) generates this fault to protect the heat exchanger. Addressing flow, mixing valves, or pump speed resolves it.
safetyWarning: Condensate from a non-condensing boiler is corrosive and can rust out the flue and heat exchanger.

fixSteps.title: Professional hydronic evaluation
fixSteps.instruction: Technician reviews system design: pump sizing, mixing valve, and primary/secondary piping.

whenToCallPro: Most boiler/water heater issues require licensed HVAC tech

faq.q: Does this apply to my mod-con?
faq.a: Mod-con boilers handle condensate, but delta-T faults still need fixing.
